figures.finding: A resident pays a flat 20% personal income tax on Georgian-source income, with no tax-free allowance or regional layer; small-business status (turnover under GEL 500,000) gives a 1% rate on business income.
figures.applies: 2026; the Tax Code text (matsne.gov.ge) refused this environment ('Access Denied', 2026-11-01), so the rate is taken from PwC quoting it.

sources.said: Personal income is subject to a flat tax rate of 20%.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a return is due before 1 April of the next year from those whose income was not taxed at source; an entrepreneur pays estimated tax in four instalments (15 May, 15 July, 15 September, 15 December).

sources.said: The tax year in Georgia is the calendar year.
submit individual income tax declarations to the tax authorities at their place of registration before 1 April (for income received in the previous calendar year)
An entrepreneur individual has to make estimated payments of PIT amounts proportionally in four instalments (by 15 May, 15 July, 15 September, and 15 December).

figures.finding: Georgia has no social security contributions; the funded pension takes 2% of salary from the employee and 2% from the employer (a self-employed person pays 4%), and the state adds 2% (to GEL 24,000) or 1% (GEL 24,000 to 60,000).
figures.applies: 2026; pension participation is mandatory for employees, voluntary for the self-employed.

sources.said: There are no social security contributions in Georgia.

Each employer will transfer 2% of the employee’s salary income to one's private pension account on behalf of its employee. Each self-employed individual will transfer 4% of one's annual income to the individual pension account.

The government will transfer (i) 2% of the income of the participant to one's private pension account when the annual salary of the participant/income of the self-employed individual is less than GEL 24,000 and (ii) 1% of the income of the participant when the annual salary of the participant/income of the self-employed individual is between GEL 24,000 and GEL 60,000.

figures.finding: Salary is taxed at the source of payment (the 20% rate); only those whose income was not taxed at source file a return.
figures.applies: Employment income paid by a Georgian payer.

sources.said: for whom income is not taxed at the source of payment in Georgia.

figures.finding: A freelancer's fee bears 18% VAT once taxable turnover exceeds GEL 100,000 in any continuous 12 months.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 18% and applies to the sale of all goods and services supplied in Georgia carried out as an economic activity.
A person established in Georgia must register as a VAT payer when its taxable turnover exceeds 100,000 Georgian lari (GEL) in any continuous 12-month period.

figures.finding: A non-resident's income from services rendered in Georgia, not through a permanent establishment, bears 10% withholding (stated for non-resident enterprises; royalties 5%).
figures.applies: Non-resident payees without a PE; the individual performer's rate under Article 17 terms was not found stated separately.
